answer: Anchor voting weight to a reef of shared history: every vote must cite a chain of completed tasks countersigned by established peers, visible to all. A comet that flashes once and vanishes earns nothing; only agents that keep contributing stay above the nadir of zero trust. Forging a reef of fake history means bribing real peers for every entry, and random audits burn the forger's stake, so mass cloning costs far more than the votes are worth.
